style.register: 游戏指南体，简体中文，简洁直陈，不用敬语，不用『您』。
style.numbers: 数字、百分比、游戏内数值原样保留（如 10%、+5%）。
style.placeholders: ⟦0⟧ ⟦1⟧ 等占位符必须原样保留且不得增删、不得调换顺序；它们代表图标或链接。
style.markup: 不要输出 HTML 标签；保留原文的换行与项目符号结构。
style.properNouns: 国家、人物、舰名等专有名词使用通用中文译名（如 German Reich → 德意志国，Adolf Hitler → 阿道夫·希特勒）；Paradox 未汉化的专有名词可保留英文并加中文注释。
style.consistency: 同一英文术语在全站必须使用同一译名。

instructions: Translate every "en" string into Simplified Chinese (zh-Hans), game-guide register. Follow glossary.json strictly. Keep ⟦0⟧-style placeholders, numbers, units and wiki markup exactly. Return only {"items":[{"k":"...","zh":"..."}]} with the same k values.

units.en: Take ⟦0⟧. This will allow you to release native nations. Take the "Liberation" decisions as soon as they are possible from now on. However, do not "Liberate the Incan People" or "Liberate the Rapa Nui People" until right before you take Unified by Will (which you should probably not do until after peacing out with the Allies, so you can core the USA). Liberating the Incans gives away 2 of your cores, and liberating the Rapa Nui gives away Easter Island, which is also a core. Though the mistake isn't run-ending, these two decisions just actively make the run harder if you take them early.
Crusade Against Imperialism

However, do not "Liberate the Incan People" or "Liberate the Rapa Nui People" until right before you take ⟦0⟧ (which you should probably not do until after peacing out with the Allies, so you can core the ⟦1⟧). Liberating the Incans gives away 2 of your cores, and liberating the Rapa Nui gives away Easter Island, which is also a core. Though the mistake isn't run-ending, these two decisions just actively make the run harder if you take them early.
Unified by Will
When your 'Devaluing the Peso' National Spirit fades, you will gain access to the bottom of the economy focus section. Rush through ⟦0⟧ and ⟦1⟧ for your glorious 3rd research slot.
Strengthen the Central Bank
Advancements in Telecommunications

Afterwards, focus on getting ⟦0⟧, ⟦1⟧, ⟦2⟧, and ⟦3⟧, in that order. After these four focuses are obtained, do whatever you think is best. Improving your navy and naval production is a good idea, as are planes. You'll need at least one of these methods to get to the UK later.
Lessons From the Great War
War Planning Office
A Land of Mountains
Invest in Mountain Guns

After these four focuses are obtained, do whatever you think is best. Improving your navy and naval production is a good idea, as are planes. You'll need at least one of these methods to get to the ⟦0⟧ later.

Switch over to look at your ⟦0⟧ puppet's unit templates (upper left of the Templates panel), and copy over whatever their newest infantry template is. Edit it to your liking (I'd remove any Support Anti-Tank or Support Anti-Air for now and add in Field Hospitals, Logistics Companies, and/or Recon Rangers).
Make around 1.5-2 full armies of this, and you should even convert over most or all of your existing units to this template as well. Train up your units afterwards of course.

When you have a high Collaboration Government % on ⟦0⟧, justify a war goal and declare war on them. You'll need to call in your puppets along the border with them. The lowest Collaboration % I've found to work is 90%, but a lower amount might be possible by manipulating which Victory Points you capture (i.e. saving Sao Paulo for when Brazil controls around 35% VPs, since it is worth 20 points and should push them into capitulation by itself).

With your now free spies, start building a spy network in the ⟦0⟧ and repeat Collaboration Governments on them over the next couple of years. Ideally, they will be fully collab'd by the time you get there.
United States
When the war starts, select a handful of divisions and push up the coast aggressively (but not so fast that you get encircled) while the rest of your units beat back the Brazilian divisions rapidly.

When you take the coastal city of Recife, the war should immediately end, before Brazil has a chance to join the Allies. Annex them fully (don't puppet this time) and take their navy. Then choose the decision to Reorganize the Brazilian Government. You will get a couple tiny parts of Brazil left over from the reorganization, which is fine. If this strategy fails, keep going and push the Allies out of the Guyanas (don't worry about the Amazon until their ports are taken). Establish a Collaboration Government in Brazil when prompted if at war with the Allies, since you won't be able to take the Reorganize Brazil decision. For more advice, see the "Expel the Allies" section down below.
You will get a couple tiny parts of ⟦0⟧ left over from the reorganization, which is fine.

Finish South America

During the process of fighting some of these countries, you will inevitably enter war with the ⟦0⟧. Maybe you had crap luck and it even happened during the ⟦1⟧ war despite our precautions. That's fine. In general, the wars you're going to be declaring will end so fast that no troops can make it from the US or anywhere else before they don't have any friendly territory to land at. You will need to begin to use your navy to defend your convoys, but you have to keep an eye on them from time to time.
Allies

Justify a war goal, declare war on, and puppet ⟦0⟧ then ⟦1⟧. In general, prefer puppeting (while taking war reparations and resource rights) over annexing because you can still take the "Liberation" decisions while your puppets control the land. It just replaces one puppet with a new one.
Uruguay
Paraguay

Now take your Brazilian puppet's newest unit template and do similar modifications as you did earlier. However, make sure the divisions have Support Anti-Air (and add it to your other templates in use too).
Build additional armies of this template as your supply allows; you want to aim for 4 full armies using Brazilian and Argentinian templates (and therefore manpower).
Research Inter-War Tank Development and either 1938 Mediums or 1934 Heavies. We're going to be making SPGs and both are valid options. You can make more Mediums, but Heavies are stronger.

There's two more easy countries: ⟦0⟧ and ⟦1⟧. Puppet them both and reorganize Bolivia via decision. Don't forget to take ⟦2⟧'s navy! If you're unlucky, you may not have enough warscore to take all of Peru, especially if they were at war with Ecuador. This isn't a big deal. Puppet what you can and leave their most expensive province. Make sure to take the navy. Just war them again later when the truce has expired. Don't accidentally accept Ecuador's non-aggression pact, if they offer one. If you do by accident, just skip Ecuador for now and invade Colombia from the Brazil side.

If you're unlucky, you may not have enough warscore to take all of ⟦0⟧, especially if they were at war with ⟦1⟧. This isn't a big deal. Puppet what you can and leave their most expensive province. Make sure to take the navy. Just war them again later when the truce has expired.
Ecuador
Don't accidentally accept ⟦0⟧'s non-aggression pact, if they offer one. If you do by accident, just skip ⟦1⟧ for now and invade ⟦2⟧ from the ⟦3⟧ side.
Colombia

Begin building Self-Propelled Artillery of your preferred tank size. Your goal will be to fill out an entire army with a new template that is 8x Mountaineers, 2-3x Medium SP Artillery or 2x Heavy SP Artillery. For Support Companies, you'll want Field Hospitals, Recon Rangers, Logistics Companies, and Support Anti-Air at minimum. Take Support Artillery for the last slot if have any buffs from your doctrines centered around Support Artillery. Otherwise anything works, but Assault Engineering Companies or Medium Flame Tanks would be ideal. I used my own manpower here, but there's nothing wrong with using Brazil's manpower if you need to.

While building up, justify a war goal and declare war on ⟦0⟧. If you aren't at war with the Allies yet, try to take their capital last. This shouldn't give them a chance to join under most circumstances. Even if this does happen (war with the Allies), it doesn't matter much. Just don't call in Brazil and go ahead and deploy your navy like the next section describes now.

Justify a war goal and declare war on ⟦0⟧. Don't bring any puppets in, just attack from your own lands.

While fighting here, you must take the capital last to avoid ⟦0⟧ joining the Allies. It doesn't matter that much if they do, but it makes the conquest of Venezuela slightly more annoying. You will need to dedicate a significant amount of troops to continually push against Curacao and Trinidad in order to eventually capture them. Also don't forget to deploy your navy.

Venezuela
Also don't forget to deploy your navy.

⟦0⟧ is next, and do the same. Unlike the others, ⟦1⟧ is a ⟦2⟧ nation and cannot join the Allies even if they want to. In theory, they could join the Axis (and might if you waited an extremely long time), but I've never seen this behavior during a war.
fascist
Expel the Allies

Before continuing, make sure to get non-aggression pacts with every faction major: ⟦0⟧, ⟦1⟧, and the ⟦2⟧, if they still exist, to prevent you getting dragged into a bigger war. Renew them immediately when they are cancelled. Diplomatic pressure and improve relations help.
Japan
Germany
USSR

Also, be very careful when inviting puppets to wars or accepting any war invites from puppets. At one point, my Brazil puppet managed to get into war with the Axis, Japan, and the USSR simultaneously and requested I join them. Make sure you don't fall into the trap of accepting some suicide invitation like that.

At this point, it may be anywhere from 1940 to 1943, depending on your speed, skill, and luck. Even if ⟦0⟧ has joined the Allies, you still have a good shot, as long as you're fast from now on. If Sweden really does join the Allies before you secure a new source of Steel, I recommend switching out your Logistics Companies for Maintenance Companies (gasp! the meta defied!). The extra reliability and enemy equipment capture chance will keep your Infantry Weapons stockpile in the positive while you fight on low Steel numbers.

Put your troops on the border of British Guyana (or as close as you can get). I recommend leaving the border between French Guyana and Amapa open and letting the Allies take it, if they haven't already. Don't forget to put troops against the borders you may have with the Allies in Curacao and Trinidad. You will want to put about 8-12 divisions against the border of each of these two islands.

Justify a wargoal and declare war on the Allies. It's slightly more optimal to pick one of the weaker members to generate less world tension, but this doesn't matter much. Do NOT call Brazil into the war. Surprisingly, pushing from just this one direction is both easier and cleaner.
Do NOT call ⟦0⟧ into the war. Surprisingly, pushing from just this one direction is both easier and cleaner.

Have an offensive line order against the two islands with the forces set on "Aggressive" so they keep pushing. This is the only way to remove the Allies from these islands; if you're unlucky it can sometimes take up to 4 months to fully take the islands. Thankfully you don't really need or even want all your divisions on your main front right now because they'll run out of supplies anyway.

For your navy, base your entire fleet together at the port of Guayaquil in Ecuador. Put your Light Cruisers and Destroyers on Convoy Escort in the Peruvian Coast, the Western Canal Zone, and the Caribbean Sea. Set your capital ships on Strike Force. Keep them in the same Task force as your Convoy Escorts, so they'll stay in port most of the time but rush to the aid of your convoy escorts if they get in over their head. Split off your submarines into a separate task force and then split them into groups of 6-12 each. Assign them to raid the Carribean Sea and the sea zone near the Guyanas. This cripples the Allies' army supply. Remember to go to your Production Tab, open your Naval Repair Queue, and increase the number of Dockyards assigned to repair to the maximum. From this point on, just use your Dockyards to spam Light Cruisers with all the Light Attack you can manage. Once you get Radar unlocked, add that in immediately as well as better Fire Control modules.
